changes.text: 格兰特收到信时还在头痛，一看到信的内容就好了。他回信说，因为他已从里士满—林奇堡路转到法姆维尔—林奇堡路，上午11点50分才拿到信；此刻在沃克教堂以西约四英里，正向前赶去会面，请对方在这条路上通知会面地点。赶到谢里登那里时，那里的人情绪激动，表示认为这是南军脱身的诡计：他们相信约翰斯顿正从北卡罗来纳北上，李要去会合；只要格兰特点头，五分钟内就能把对方打垮。格兰特不怀疑李的诚意，不久便被领到李所在之处。

The officer found Grant still suffering with the sick headache; in Grant's own telling, "the instant I saw the contents of the note I was cured." He wrote back at once. Lee's note had reached him only at 11:50 a.m., he explained, because he had passed from the Richmond and Lynchburg road to the Farmville and Lynchburg road; he was at that moment about four miles west of Walker's Church and would push forward to the front for the meeting; a message left on this road naming the place would reach him. When he rode up to Sheridan's position, the men there were very much excited. They expressed their view that the whole thing was a ruse to let the Confederates get away. Johnston, they believed, was marching up from North Carolina and Lee moving to join him, and they would whip the rebels where they stood in five minutes if only Grant would let them go in. Grant had no doubt of Lee's good faith, and was soon conducted to where he was.
会面在阿波马托克斯考特豪斯一位麦克莱恩先生的房子里，李带着参谋马歇尔上校等在那里。格兰特当天一早离营时没料到结果来得这么快，因此穿着很随便：士兵短上衣，肩上钉着军衔肩章以示身份；也没带佩剑，他骑马在战场上时通常就不带。

The meeting took place at the house of a Mr. McLean at Appomattox Court House, where Lee waited with Colonel Marshall, one of his staff officers. Grant had left camp that morning with no inkling that the end would come so quickly, and so he was in rough garb: a soldier's blouse for a coat, with the shoulder straps of his rank so the army would know who he was, and no sword, as he usually went without one when riding the field.
李写信接受条件，说条款与格兰特8日来信中所提的实质相同，他将指定军官来办交接。在告辞之前，他说自己的军队状况很糟：缺粮，没有草料，士兵连日只吃炒玉米，需要请格兰特供应口粮和草料。格兰特说当然可以，问需要多少人的口粮，李答约两万五千人；格兰特便让李派自己的军需官和军需主任到两三英里外的阿波马托克斯车站，从被截停的列车上取用所需。

Lee wrote accepting the terms: being substantially the same as those expressed in Grant's letter of the 8th, they were accepted, and he would designate the proper officers to carry the stipulations into effect. Before taking his leave he added that his army was in a very bad condition for want of food, and without forage; his men had been living for days on parched corn exclusively, and he would have to ask Grant for rations and forage. Grant agreed at once and asked how many men needed rations; about twenty-five thousand, Lee answered. Grant authorized him to send his own commissary and quartermaster to Appomattox Station, two or three miles away, where out of the trains the Union had stopped they could have all the provisions wanted.
格兰特回信说，他没有谈和的权限，南方放下武器就能让和平早日到来。此后李再次来信，可这封信送得很费劲：由于格兰特所走的路线，对方很可能无法在约定时间内联系上他并带回答复。米德和谢里登都对是否停火非常犹豫，怕这不是真心求和；而且北弗吉尼亚军团已无路可逃，除非用诡计脱身。因为路线的缘故，李派人护送带信的军官穿过自己的战线，把信送到格兰特手里。

Grant replied that he had no authority to treat on the subject of peace, and that by laying down their arms the South would hasten peace. Lee then wrote again, but this message was hard to deliver: from the route Grant had taken, Lee's side would probably not be able to reach him and get an answer back within the time fixed. Meade and Sheridan both hesitated very considerably about suspending hostilities at all. They were afraid the overture was not in good faith; and the Army of Northern Virginia was where it could not escape except by some deception. Because of Grant's route, Lee sent an escort with the officer bearing the message through his own lines to Grant.
又谈了几句，李再次打断话头，建议把条件写成文字。格兰特叫他幕中担任秘书的帕克将军取来纸笔，开始写。他后来说，落笔时连第一个词该写什么都不知道，只想着把自己心里的意思表达清楚，让人不会误会；写到一半，想起军官的私马和私物对他们很重要，对己方却毫无用处，而要他们交出佩刀是不必要的羞辱。

They talked on a little longer, and then Lee interrupted again to suggest that the terms ought to be written out. Grant called to General Parker, secretary on his staff, for writing materials and began to write. As he later told it, when he put pen to paper he did not know the first word he should use. He knew only what was in his mind and wanted to express it clearly, so there could be no mistaking it. As he wrote on, it occurred to him that the officers had private horses and effects that were important to them and of no value to the Union, and that "it would be an unnecessary humiliation to call upon them to deliver their side arms."
马骡那条更实际。格兰特当场给出的理由是过冬的收成：收缴来的牲口对联邦没用，对回家的小农是活下去的工具。一种解释是，这一条针对的不是面子，而是协议签完之后能不能真的收场——人要回乡、要吃饭、要种地，前面那些条款才有执行的人。要提醒的是，这一项不在已写成的条文里，是格兰特当面答应李、将指示留守军官办理的。

The horses and mules were the more practical item. The reason Grant gave on the spot was the winter crop: animals taken in surrender were of no use to the Union, but to small farmers going home they were the tools of survival. One reading is that this clause addressed not face but whether the settlement could actually be wound up afterward — the men had to go home, eat, and plant, and only then were there people to carry out everything already written down. A caution: this was not in the terms as written; Grant told Lee he would instruct the officers left behind.
马骡的宽许不在已写成的条文里，是格兰特当面对李承诺、将指示留守军官办理的；落实得如何，原文没有交代；名册、宣誓这些条件怎样逐项执行，同样没有记载。日期只按原文「the 8th」这样的写法转述，不补出原文没有的年份。

The indulgence on horses and mules was not in the terms as written; Grant promised Lee he would instruct the officers left behind to allow it. How far it was carried out the source does not say, and neither does it record how the rolls and paroles were executed item by item. Dates are kept as the source has them — "the 8th" and the like — with no year added that the original does not give.
全文只有一个史源，即格兰特本人的回忆记述。对话是他的转述，未必逐字；他明言不知李的心情；本文不替任何一方补写心理；马匹宽许不在已写成的条文中，是格兰特当面答应李将指示留守军官办理的，其落实情况以及名册与宣誓的逐项执行，原文均未交代；日期按原文写法，不补年份。

There is only one source for this piece: Grant's own account in his memoirs. The conversations are his retellings and need not be verbatim; he says expressly that he did not know Lee's feelings, and this piece does not supply psychology for either side; the allowance on horses and mules was not in the written terms but promised to Lee as an instruction to the officers left behind, and neither its implementation nor the item-by-item execution of the rolls and paroles is reported; dates are kept in the original wording, with no year supplied.
至于叫停鸣炮，一种解释是，受降条件里最后一项从不写在纸上：胜利方当天说的第一句话。作者提出的替代做法是，把收缴佩刀之类的要求当作威慑保留下来，让对方记住谁说了算；代价可能是执行阶段对方不愿配合，因为真正要办的事——交名册、办宣誓、放人回乡——都得靠对方的人去做。

As for halting the salute, one reading is that the last clause of any surrender is never set on paper: it is the first thing the winning side says that day. The alternative the writer offers is to keep demands such as handing over side-arms on the books as a reminder of who is in charge. The cost might be an unwillingness to cooperate in the carrying out, because the things that genuinely have to be done — delivering the rolls, taking the paroles, sending the men home — depend on the other side's people doing them.

dispositions.rationale: 英文把“His note”改为“Lee's note”，明确11点50分收到的是李的来信。中文原无歧义，未改动此句。

evidence.quote: Your note of this date is but this moment (11.50 A.M.) received

dispositions.rationale: 中文补上“穿着很随便”的总括，并说明他骑马在战场上时通常不带剑，与英文和原文一致。

evidence.quote: consequently was in rough garb. I was without a sword, as I usually was when on horseback on the field

dispositions.rationale: 英文删去“— the courthouse village —”。中文改为音译地名“阿波马托克斯考特豪斯”，不再说明地名性质；同时按原文补上马歇尔的上校衔，与英文一致。

evidence.quote: at the house of a Mr. McLean, at Appomattox Court House, with Colonel Marshall

dispositions.rationale: 删去“随即”和“promptly”。证据只给出接受信的内容，没有交代写信时间。

evidence.quote: As they are substantially the same as those expressed in your letter of the 8th inst., they are accepted.

dispositions.rationale: 英文把“since”改为“; and”，中文把冒号改为“；而且”，恢复原文的并列关系，不再暗示两者之间有因果。

evidence.quote: They were afraid it was not in good faith, and we had the Army of Northern Virginia where it could not escape except by some deception

dispositions.rationale: 中文改为“他幕中担任秘书的帕克将军”，与英文和原文一致。中文末尾嵌入的英文原句违反中文正文不嵌英文的规则，已删去，只保留已有的中文转述，事实不变。英文未改。

evidence.quote: I called to General Parker, secretary on my staff, for writing materials

dispositions.rationale: 中文补上格兰特询问需要多少人口粮、李答约两万五千人这一问一答，与英文和原文一致。

evidence.quote: I told him "certainly," and asked for how many men he wanted rations. His answer was "about twenty-five thousand;"

dispositions.rationale: 删去“只是口头指示”的断言。改为：这一项不在已写成的条文里，是格兰特当面答应李、将指示留守军官办理的。

evidence.quote: I told him that as the terms were written they would not
I would, therefore, instruct the officers I left behind to receive the paroles of his troops

dispositions.rationale: 中英文都去掉“口头指示”的说法，改为：宽许不在已写成的条文里，是格兰特当面承诺将指示留守军官办理的。

evidence.quote: I would, therefore, instruct the officers I left behind

dispositions.rationale: 中英文都去掉“只是口头指示”和“verbal only”，改为：不在已写成的条文中，是格兰特当面答应李、将指示留守军官办理的。

evidence.quote: as the terms were written they would not

dispositions.rationale: 中文把“无人配合”改为“对方不愿配合”，与英文“an unwillingness to cooperate”的保留程度一致。英文未改。
中文改为“表示认为”，英文改为“They expressed their view that”，忠实于原文的转述语气。

evidence.quote: expressed their view that this was all a ruse employed to enable the Confederates to get away
